Definition: middle voice of a compound of G1223 and G950; to confirm thoroughly (by words), i.e. asseverate:--affirm constantly.
BiblicalUsage: To affirm constantly is to insist on a thing with all the weight you can put behind it. Paul tells Titus to affirm the good works of believers, and he tells Timothy that some who teach the law affirm what they do not understand.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that there is a difference between affirming truth and merely insisting on an opinion; Paul wants Titus to press home what is good and true, and he warns Timothy that loud certainty is no substitute for knowing what you are talking about.
